title: Identify High-Net-Worth Customers with Multiple Accounts
description_markdown: Business request: Identify customers who have an aggregated bank balance across all their accounts strictly greater than $50,000. Return `c.name`, `c.email`, and their total balance `SUM(a.balance)` as `total_balance`. Order by `total_balance` DESC, `c.customer_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Sum balances per customer with HAVING > 50000
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT c.name, c.email, SUM(a.balance) AS total_balance FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name, c.email HAVING SUM(a.balance) > 50000.00 ORDER BY total_balance DESC, c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins accounts to customer master and filters combined balances using HAVING.
hints: Join `bank_customers c` and `accounts a` on `c.customer_id = a.customer_id`.
Filter with `HAVING SUM(a.balance) > 50000.00`.

Query: SELECT c.name, c.email, SUM(a.balance) AS total_balance FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name, c.email HAVING SUM(a.balance) > 50000.00 ORDER BY total_balance DESC, c.customer_id ASC;

title: Calculate Branch Total Deposits and Account Liquidity
description_markdown: Business request: For each branch in `branches`, calculate the total number of accounts managed as `account_count`, and the total customer deposits held as `total_deposits`. Return `b.branch_name`, `b.city`, `account_count`, and `total_deposits`. Order by `total_deposits` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Aggregate accounts by branch
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT b.branch_name, b.city, COUNT(a.account_id) AS account_count, COALESCE(SUM(a.balance), 0) AS total_deposits FROM branches b LEFT JOIN accounts a ON b.branch_id = a.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id, b.branch_name, b.city ORDER BY total_deposits DESC, b.branch_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses LEFT JOIN to ensure branches with zero accounts report zero balance.
hints: Use `LEFT JOIN accounts a ON b.branch_id = a.branch_id`.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT b.branch_name, b.city, COUNT(a.account_id) AS account_count, COALESCE(SUM(a.balance), 0) AS total_deposits FROM branches b LEFT JOIN accounts a ON b.branch_id = a.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id, b.branch_name, b.city ORDER BY total_deposits DESC, b.branch_id ASC;

title: Flag Transactions Exceeding Account Balance Threshold
description_markdown: Compliance audit request: Find all completed transactions where the transaction amount is strictly greater than $5,000. Join with `accounts` and `bank_customers`. Return `t.transaction_id`, `c.name AS customer_name`, `t.transaction_type`, and `t.amount`. Order by `t.amount` DESC, `t.transaction_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Audit large transactions > 5000
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT t.transaction_id, c.name AS customer_name, t.transaction_type, t.amount FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON t.account_id = a.account_id JOIN bank_customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE t.amount > 5000.00 AND t.status = 'completed' ORDER BY t.amount DESC, t.transaction_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Filters for AML compliance reporting on large transaction velocity.
hints: Join transactions -> accounts -> bank_customers.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT t.transaction_id, c.name AS customer_name, t.transaction_type, t.amount FROM transactions t JOIN accounts a ON t.account_id = a.account_id JOIN bank_customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE t.amount > 5000.00 AND t.status = 'completed' ORDER BY t.amount DESC, t.transaction_id ASC;

title: Find Active Checking Accounts with High Balance
description_markdown: Query customer names, account IDs, and balances for all checking accounts with a balance of at least $1,000.00. Order by `balance` DESC, then `account_id` ASC.

solution_query: SELECT c.name, a.account_id, a.balance FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE a.account_type = 'checking' AND a.balance >= 1000.00 ORDER BY a.balance DESC, a.account_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins bank_customers to accounts filtering by checking account_type and minimum balance.
hints: Join `bank_customers c` and `accounts a` on `c.customer_id = a.customer_id`.
Filter with `WHERE a.account_type = 'checking' AND a.balance >= 1000.00`.

Query: SELECT c.name, a.account_id, a.balance FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE a.account_type = 'checking' AND a.balance >= 1000.00 ORDER BY a.balance DESC, a.account_id ASC;

description_markdown: Aggregate total accounts and sum of balances grouped by `account_type`. Order by `total_balance` DESC, `account_type` ASC.

hints: Use `GROUP BY account_type`.

hints: Filter using `joined_date >= '2021-01-01' AND joined_date <= '2021-12-31'`.
Select `customer_id`, `name`, and `joined_date`.
Query: SELECT customer_id, name, joined_date FROM bank_customers WHERE joined_date >= '2021-01-01' AND joined_date <= '2021-12-31' ORDER BY joined_date ASC, customer_id ASC;

title: Find Highest Single Account Balance per Branch

solution_query: SELECT b.branch_name, MAX(a.balance) AS max_balance FROM branches b JOIN accounts a ON b.branch_id = a.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id, b.branch_name ORDER BY max_balance DESC, b.branch_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins branches and accounts and computes MAX(balance) grouped by branch.
hints: Join `branches b` and `accounts a` on `b.branch_id = a.branch_id`.

title: Analyze Completed Transaction Volumes by Transaction Type

hints: Filter with `WHERE status = 'completed'`.
Group by `transaction_type` and aggregate count and sum.

title: Classify Customers into Credit Risk Tiers
description_markdown: Classify each customer's credit score using CASE: 'Excellent' for >= 750, 'Good' for >= 680, and 'Fair' otherwise as `credit_tier`. Order by `credit_score` DESC, `customer_id` ASC.

-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT customer_id, name, credit_score, CASE WHEN credit_score >= 750 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN credit_score >= 680 THEN 'Good' ELSE 'Fair' END AS credit_tier FROM bank_customers ORDER BY credit_score DESC, customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses conditional CASE statement to map credit scores into tiers.
hints: Use `CASE WHEN credit_score >= 750 THEN 'Excellent' ... END`.

Query: SELECT customer_id, name, credit_score, CASE WHEN credit_score >= 750 THEN 'Excellent' WHEN credit_score >= 680 THEN 'Good' ELSE 'Fair' END AS credit_tier FROM bank_customers ORDER BY credit_score DESC, customer_id ASC;

title: Detect Dormant Accounts with Zero Transactions
description_markdown: Identify all bank accounts that have never recorded a single transaction. Return `account_id`, `account_type`, and `balance`. Order by `account_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT a.account_id, a.account_type, a.balance FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL ORDER BY a.account_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Performs an anti-join using LEFT JOIN and filtering WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL.
hints: LEFT JOIN `transactions t` on `a.account_id = t.account_id`.
Filter with `WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL`.
Query: SELECT a.account_id, a.account_type, a.balance FROM accounts a LEFT JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.transaction_id IS NULL ORDER BY a.account_id ASC;

title: Identify Customers Holding Both Checking and Savings Accounts
description_markdown: Find customers who own both a 'checking' and a 'savings' account. Return `customer_id` and `name`. Order by `customer_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE a.account_type IN ('checking', 'savings') GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_type) = 2 ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Groups customer accounts and requires COUNT(DISTINCT account_type) = 2 for checking and savings.
hints: Filter `account_type IN ('checking', 'savings')`.
Group by customer and filter with `HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_type) = 2`.

Query: SELECT c.customer_id, c.name FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id WHERE a.account_type IN ('checking', 'savings') GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_type) = 2 ORDER BY c.customer_id ASC;

title: Rank Accounts Within Each Branch by Liquidity
description_markdown: For each branch, rank its accounts from highest balance to lowest balance using `DENSE_RANK()` as `balance_rank`. Return `branch_name`, `account_id`, `balance`, and `balance_rank`. Order by `branch_name` ASC, `balance_rank` ASC, `account_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT b.branch_name, a.account_id, a.balance, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.branch_id ORDER BY a.balance DESC) AS balance_rank FROM accounts a JOIN branches b ON a.branch_id = b.branch_id ORDER BY b.branch_name ASC, balance_rank ASC, a.account_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses DENSE_RANK() partitioned by branch_id ordered by balance DESC.
hints: Use `DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.branch_id ORDER BY a.balance DESC)`.
Join `accounts` to `branches` on `branch_id`.

Query: SELECT b.branch_name, a.account_id, a.balance, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.branch_id ORDER BY a.balance DESC) AS balance_rank FROM accounts a JOIN branches b ON a.branch_id = b.branch_id ORDER BY b.branch_name ASC, balance_rank ASC, a.account_id ASC;

title: Calculate Cumulative Account Deposit Volume Over Time
description_markdown: For all completed deposits, calculate the running total of deposited money per account as `cumulative_deposits`. Return `transaction_id`, `account_id`, `amount`, and `cumulative_deposits`. Order by `account_id` ASC, `tx_time` ASC, `transaction_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT transaction_id, account_id, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC) AS cumulative_deposits FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'deposit' ORDER BY account_id ASC, tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC;

hints: Filter with `WHERE transaction_type = 'deposit'`.
Use `SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC)`.

Query: SELECT transaction_id, account_id, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC) AS cumulative_deposits FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'deposit' ORDER BY account_id ASC, tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC;

title: Find Customers with Average Account Balance Above $20,000
description_markdown: Compute the average account balance across all accounts owned by each customer. Return `customer_id`, `name`, and `avg_balance` for customers whose average balance strictly exceeds $20,000.00. Order by `avg_balance` DESC, `customer_id` ASC.

-- Write your solution query here

title: Determine the Largest Transaction Processed per Customer
description_markdown: Identify the maximum completed transaction amount executed by each customer as `max_amount`. Return `name` and `max_amount`. Order by `max_amount` DESC, `name` ASC.

solution_query: SELECT c.name, MAX(t.amount) AS max_amount FROM bank_customers c JOIN accounts a ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id JOIN transactions t ON a.account_id = t.account_id WHERE t.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.name ORDER BY max_amount DESC, c.name ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins bank_customers, accounts, and transactions to find MAX(amount) per customer.
hints: Join `bank_customers`, `accounts`, and `transactions`.

title: Compute Net Transaction Cashflow by Account
description_markdown: Calculate net cashflow per account (deposits minus withdrawals) for completed transactions as `net_cashflow`. Return `account_id` and `net_cashflow`. Order by `net_cashflow` DESC, `account_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net_cashflow FROM transactions WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY net_cashflow DESC, account_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Uses conditional SUM with CASE statement to subtract withdrawals from deposits.
hints: Use `SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END)`.
Group by `account_id`.

Query: SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'deposit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END) AS net_cashflow FROM transactions WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY net_cashflow DESC, account_id ASC;

solution_query: SELECT account_id, account_type, balance FROM accounts WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts) ORDER BY balance DESC, account_id ASC;

hints: Compare balance using `WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts)`.
Order by `balance` DESC, `account_id` ASC.
Query: SELECT account_id, account_type, balance FROM accounts WHERE balance > (SELECT AVG(balance) FROM accounts) ORDER BY balance DESC, account_id ASC;

title: Track Previous Transaction Amount per Account Using LAG
description_markdown: For each transaction, display the previous transaction's amount on that same account as `prev_amount` using `LAG()`. Return `transaction_id`, `account_id`, `amount`, and `prev_amount`. Order by `account_id` ASC, `tx_time` ASC, `transaction_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here

solution_query: SELECT transaction_id, account_id, amount, LAG(amount, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC) AS prev_amount FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id ASC, tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Applies LAG(amount, 1) partitioned by account_id ordered chronologically.
hints: Use `LAG(amount, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC)`.

Query: SELECT transaction_id, account_id, amount, LAG(amount, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC) AS prev_amount FROM transactions ORDER BY account_id ASC, tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC;

title: Calculate Balance Variance from Branch Average

title: Compute Global Running Total of Completed Transactions

solution_explanation: Calculates running total using SUM() OVER (ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC).
hints: Filter completed transactions with `WHERE status = 'completed'`.
Use window function `SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY tx_time ASC, transaction_id ASC)`.
